**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Formal/mathematical logic papers: non-classical and algebraic logics remain the core profile, alongside proof theory, model theory, modal/many-valued/substructural/connexive logics, and applications of formal logic to philosophy, methodology of science, and linguistics. Recent (2022-2026) article titles found via search include 'An Algebraic Investigation of the Connexive Logic C', 'On Boolean Algebraic Structure of Proofs: Towards an Algebraic Semantics for the Logic of Proofs', and papers in active 2025-2026 special issues on paraconsistency, contemporary logic in Brazil, and a memorial issue on Constantine Tsinakis (algebraic/substructural logic).

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** algebraic logic / abstract algebraic logic, proof theory, modal and many-valued logics, substructural and connexive logics, non-classical logics generally, model theory applied to logic, formal epistemology, applications of formal logic to philosophy, methodology of science, linguistics, cognitive science
